failedObligations.finding: The service mechanics are right and the objection clock is wrong in a way that can mislead a felony-class petitioner. Correct: two recipients from the form's own Certificate of Service (the prosecuting or city attorney, and the arresting agency), the form's two methods, and the rule that the certificate is completed only after service. The defect is the objection window. The packet leads with a flat "The prosecuting attorney has 30 days to object", sourced to the committed packet-set manifest. I traced that sentence: it is data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/AR.memo.json rules.service, and it appears VERBATIM on 11 of the 12 Arkansas tracks in that file — including ar-felony-seal, where the same repository's compiled profile says the window is 90 days. A line that is provably wrong on a sibling track it is attached to is state-level boilerplate, not a route-addressed determination, and under A3 (holding is per FACT, not per document) it does not establish this route's answer. The record that DOES address it is the compiled profile's own table: "Prosecutor objection window - misdemeanor 30 days / felony 90 days, Receipt / filing of petition". That rule is self-applying here, because the delivered petition prints "A Class _____ [_] felony [_] misdemeanor" and the participant supplies the class. So the repository establishes a determinate class-keyed rule and the packet publishes a flat number from a non-route-held line, demoting the real rule to "the longer window MAY apply to you". It then sends a statutory question to an office that cannot answer it: "ask the clerk of the court where you file which window that court runs" — the window is set by statute, not by court practice, and A1 permits a named authority to stand in only where no held source establishes the fact. The contrast is inside this same builder's own work: ar-misdemeanor-dwi-seal-set resolves the identical conflict correctly by naming its route's class ("this packet is a misdemeanour DWI or BWI conviction, which puts it in the 30-day limb"). The repair is one paragraph: state the class rule as the rule, cite the profile, and drop the clerk sentence. Recorded separately: the three-day service deadline comes only from that same 11-track boilerplate — the compiled profile contains no "three days" and the form prints none — but it errs toward serving early, so I record it as a provenance limit rather than a failure.

The filing instructions page states: 'No committed record this packet binds states a filing fee, or a fee waiver, for this route. The office that answers both is the clerk's office of the Mississippi court that granted nonadjudication…'. The profile it binds carries sourceSections[2], title 'Filing Fee', category 'fees': 'Mississippi Code 99-19-72 sets a $150 filing fee for each petition to expunge an offense under 99-19-71' and 'Expect at least a $150 statutory filing fee for many 99-19-71 petitions, but confirm with the clerk'. The same profile's packetGenerator.feeRules carries the same three lines. And the packet's own petition page tells the participant, quoting that profile, that the operative provision 'appears in both Sec. 99-15-26(5) and Sec. 99-19-71(4)'. Having told the participant the provision is shared with § 99-19-71, the packet cannot then say no bound record states a fee and send them to the clerk: that is the sibling fee trap A4 records, and it is not walked around. The comparison that settles it is inside this same lane: ms-misd-addl-set, built for §§ 9-11-15(3) and 21-23-7(6) where no such overlap is even asserted, devotes an entire block to naming the $150, naming § 99-19-72, and stating why it does not reach — 'THIS PETITION IS NOT BROUGHT UNDER SEC. 99-19-71 … the Sec. 99-19-72 fee does not reach those sections by its terms.' This packet, which has the stronger overlap, names neither section and neither figure. NOTE FOR THE REPAIR: A3 forbids the opposite error just as firmly. The repair is NOT to state that $150 applies to a § 99-15-26(5) petition. It is to name § 99-19-72 and § 99-19-71, state on this route's own terms whether the fee reaches it, and say what the record does and does not settle.

The office of the court with jurisdiction over the matter is the authority that can answer both' — names two facts, the fee and how the court accepts a filing, which step five confirms by pairing 'how it accepts filings' with 'the right court'. Neither is the service question, and A3's per-fact discipline cuts the same way against a packet as against a repository: an authority named for the delivery-method fact does not answer whether anyone must be served. On the repository side I confirmed nothing is held: the route contract has no service key at all (its keys are jurisdiction, decisionId, ruleId, routeKey, pathwayId, mechanism, statute, stage, outcomeMode, timing, requiredFacts, screeningFactIds, exclusions, packetFamily, packetComponents, notes, and the string 'serv' does not occur in it); there is no packet-set manifest entry for this family; and the only notice rule in the compiled Mississippi profile — 'The petitioner must give 10 days written notice to the district attorney before any hearing' — is cited to law.justia.com section-99-19-71 and is keyed to § 99-19-71, so A3 bars reading it across to § 99-15-59. So this is not an A1 failure to state a held fact. It is the silence limb: nothing held, and nothing said.

failedObligations.evidence: The legal decision's Mechanism section (sha256 17ae635a4e434bc04fd65fc0bb7d6cda551922064d6dfb990fa240f437f7db29) states: 'Use the official Alabama AOC Order of Limited Relief packet, including the sworn petition and proposed order.' The census records participantFacingInstrument as 'official Alabama AOC Order of Limited Relief sworn petition and proposed order'. The build worklist records deliverable.proposedOrder with status 'recorded' and entry 'official AOC proposed order'. product-wiring.json declares one component, role primary_filing, documentId AL-AOC-C-94A-PETITION-FOR-ORDER-OF-LIMITED-RELIEF, and the family renders two fixtures of that one document. Extracting each of the three pages of petition-canonical-filled.pdf shows page 1 the petition caption and sworn statements, page 2 the Act's notes and the conviction/consequence list, page 3 RETURN ON SERVICE. There is no order page anywhere in the packet. Nor is the absence declared: build-findings.json carries blocking [] and findingCount 0, the receipt's whatThisReceiptDoesNotEstablish says nothing about it, and participant-instructions.md asserts positively 'This packet is one form' and closes 'This is a prepared copy of the Alabama Unified Judicial System's own Form C-94A.' A participant reading this packet has no way to learn that the record for their route calls for a proposed order as well. Contrast the MS nonadjudication family in this same lane, which names each component the route contract lists and states which of them is a record the participant obtains rather than a page the packet composes — that is a declared disposition; this is a silent one.

The decision records six refer-to-counsel conditions. Five are carried: a prohibited offence or registration consequence, an out-of-state jurisdiction with no clear comparable relief, joinder across counties, an agency contesting the requested limitation, and a petition asking to eliminate a consequence chapter 12-26 does not authorise the court to override. The sixth is absent: 'the collateral consequence is not identified with specificity.' Grepping participant-instructions.md case-insensitively for 'specific', 'with specificity', 'identify … consequence' and 'which consequence' returns nothing, and the same grep over the extracted text of both fixtures returns nothing. This is not an incidental omission on this route: the whole relief is defined by which named collateral consequence is being lifted, the packet itself leaves that list entirely to the participant across five ruled lines, and a vague list is the single most likely way a petition of this kind fails. The packet carries instead the build worklist's condensed handoff sentence, which happens not to include the specificity limb, so the fuller record the census names for this route reaches the participant incompletely.

failedObligations.finding: Three sentences print a POINTER in the grammatical position of the FACT, and the packet's own design turns that into a participant-facing defect. In all four tracks, paragraph 5 reads "Applicant was charged with Possession offense shown on the certified disposition by [ARRESTING AGENCY MUST BE CONFIRMED]", paragraph 7 reads "The matter was resolved with the following disposition: Disposition shown on the certified disposition", and paragraph 8 reads "Applicant may be eligible for sealing on the following basis: Eligibility is not certified by this artifact; source review and local-court confirmation are required." The first two state where to find a fact in the slot where the fact belongs; the third puts the factory's own non-certification language into a pleading's eligibility allegation. This matters because of what the instructions ask the participant to do with the document: "Transfer only reviewed content to that form." The bracketed ALL-CAPS markers are self-evidently not transferable and the top-level instructions name every one of them and say what to supply instead. These three sentences carry no such marking, sit in ordinary prose, and are not transferable content — paragraph 8 is affirmatively wrong to copy onto a court form. The fix is to mark them as unresolved in the same way the bracketed items are, or to omit the clause rather than print a pointer as an allegation.

failedObligations.finding: The packet denies a rule the repository states, and the denial costs the participant a real limb. It says: "No held source in this packet names a statewide Ohio filing office or a statewide application." Under A2 the repository includes the compiled state profile, and src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/OH-ohio.json states the rule plainly and repeatedly, keyed to these sections: "File in the sentencing court for an Ohio conviction or in a court of common pleas for an out-of-state or federal conviction", and for § 2953.35 "The application is filed in the sentencing court". A1 as amended settles the order of operations — ask first whether the repository establishes the answer; if it does, the packet states it. The consequence is not cosmetic: the packet's substitute answer, "the Ohio court that handled the case", silently drops the out-of-state and federal conviction limb, and a participant in that position is sent to a court that is not in Ohio at all. The repair is to state the profile's two-limb rule.

failedObligations.finding: The clearest of the four, because the profile answers this route by statute number. The packet says: "No held source in this packet states a filing fee, states that filing is free, or states a fee-waiver procedure ... This packet does not state an amount because it holds no source for one." The compiled Ohio profile carries a route-keyed fee table that I read in this lane: "Route Fee | 2953.32 conviction/bail forfeiture sealing or expungement | $50 application fee unless indigent, plus possible local court fee up to $50 | Dismissal / not guilty / no bill sealing | Ohio Legal Help says no fee | ... | 2953.35 firearm/carry expungement | $50 unless indigent". Three of this family's four tracks are answered by section number — § 2953.32 twice and § 2953.35 — and the fourth, § 2953.33 non-conviction relief, is answered by the disposition row for dismissals, not-guilty and no-bill cases. The indigency waiver the packet says it holds no source for is named in the same table and again in the § 2953.35 text ("The fee is $50 unless indigent"). This is per-fact, per-route holding in A3's own terms — the table is keyed by statutory section and the sections match — so none of it is a sibling-route inference. The packet is silent about something the repository knows, and "ask the clerk" substitutes a question for an answer we have.

failedObligations.finding: The packet says "No held source in this packet states who must be served or how. Ask the same clerk." The profile states the mechanism, keyed to these sections: the court sets and holds the hearing 45 to 90 days after filing, and "The prosecutor may object at least 30 days before the hearing, and victims may be heard if applicable" — recorded against § 2953.32/.321 and, separately, "The court holds a hearing 45-90 days after filing, and the prosecutor may object" against § 2953.33. The honest answer is materially better for the participant than the question the packet asks in its place: on this scheme the applicant serves nobody, the court notifies, and there is a stated window to expect. That is the same shape as the correction already applied to a New York family in this factory, where the packet was repaired to state affirmatively that the court distributes and the participant serves nobody. Telling a participant to go and ask who to serve, when the held answer is that they serve no one, leaves them looking for a step that does not exist.

The compiled Utah state profile carries 'Path B - Automatic Expungement: Acquittal or Dismissal With Prejudice' and, in its own words, 'Acquittal on all charges Goal: 60 days after acquittal for qualifying post-May 1, 2020 cases', together with 'As of January 1, 2026 ... the court identifies and clears eligible automatic-expungement cases on its own'. Neither participant-instructions.md nor the delivered canonical bytes contain the words automatic, Clean Slate, 60 days or any equivalent: grep for 'automatic|clean slate|60 day|60-day|120 day' returns zero hits in both. The packet instead directs the participant to pay a non-refundable $65.00 to BCI and $150 to the court. Under A2 the compiled state profile is a held source, and under A3 these lines address this route's own fact pattern -- acquittal -- rather than a sibling statute, so this is not a sibling-route inference. The repair is to state the automatic route and the check before the fee paragraphs, not to remove the petition route.

failedObligations.finding: The A4 defect is repaired; a second one behind it is not. Repaired, and I confirmed it: the packet now states "The BCI application fee is $65.00, and it is non-refundable", quotes both printed instances, and states the indigency waiver and its sequencing rule (the waiver form must be completed BEFORE applying, and BCI will not process the application until it arrives). The NARROWED refusal also satisfies A4 because it names its subject — it is "The certificates themselves ... this packet does not state that amount", explicitly distinguished from the application fee — which is exactly the combination A4 called for, and it names BCI as the office to ask. What fails is the substance of that refusal against the repository. src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/UT-utah.json records BCI's own FAQ: "eligible conviction, plea-in-abeyance, or special certificates may require an additional $65 per case; no certificate issuance fee is required for dismissals, acquittals, or declinations." For THIS route the held figure is $65 per case. So the packet's "this packet does not state that amount because BCI sets it per applicant" denies a figure the repository holds, and its companion sentence "The certificates themselves cost more than the application" is contradicted by that figure for a single-incident conviction, where the certificate equals the $65 application fee rather than exceeding it. Under A3 this line is on-route: it is keyed by disposition class and names convictions. Stated as a residual: the profile's "may require" is genuinely conditional and BCI's letter remains the operative per-applicant statement, so the repair is to state the held $65-per-case figure and its condition and keep BCI as the confirming authority — not to promise a total.

failedObligations.finding: Two limbs, and the first is the harder one the Captain asked me to test. (1) The certificate refusal is not merely narrow on this route; it is false, and false in the expensive direction. The packet carries the same paragraph as its conviction sibling, word for word: "The certificates themselves cost more than the application, and this packet does not state that amount because BCI sets it per applicant." The compiled Utah profile records BCI's FAQ as: "eligible conviction, plea-in-abeyance, or special certificates may require an additional $65 per case; NO CERTIFICATE ISSUANCE FEE IS REQUIRED FOR DISMISSALS, ACQUITTALS, OR DECLINATIONS." This route is a dismissal. The line is keyed by disposition class and names dismissals expressly, so it is on-route under A3 — unlike the California trap A3 was written for, there is no competing statutory section here, and unlike the West Virginia trap there is no sibling remedy being borrowed. So the repository establishes that the certificate issuance fee is ZERO for this route, and the packet tells the participant it is MORE than $65 and unknowable. That is not a refusal that A1 permits; it is a positive misstatement of a held fact, and it overstates the cost of the route the participant is holding. The identical wording across both Utah families shows why: the fee text was written once for the conviction route and reused unchanged where the disposition class inverts the answer. (2) The free-alternative paragraph omits its own exclusion. The packet tells the participant, in bold, "there is a free route to the same result ... automatic expungement 180 days after the dismissal under Utah Code 77-40a-206, where no appeal was filed", and "If you are not in a hurry, waiting out the 180 days is free." The profile states the carve-out twice, and the packet never mentions it: a dismissal with prejudice following a successful plea in abeyance is excluded from that automatic category. A participant in that position is advised to wait 180 days for relief that will not arrive, having been told their paid petition is merely the faster route to the same end. The disclosure is otherwise admirable — it argues against the packet's own sale — which is precisely why it needs its exclusion.

failedObligations.finding: The packet tells the participant that it does not state an amount that its own delivered pages print. participant-instructions.md carries, in bold: "The BCI certificate carries a separate fee, and this packet does not state an amount because BCI sets it per applicant." The canonical fixture this family ships prints "$65.00" three times on packet pages 17 and 18, on the BCI Application for Certificate of Eligibility the packet itself delivers. Confirmed in this lane with pdftotext against this family's own committed bytes (SHA-256 86290244b6882ee9bb403b2b3fff4035d136abf33352b9c8fcb064eb125c3c0f), not taken from any brief or report. DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 amendment A4 states the rule in one line: a packet may never tell a participant that it does not state something it does state. A SECOND and independent limb fails here too. The compiled Utah state profile (src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/UT-utah.json, SHA-256 73dd7ea988d0673dca3b8bf657f2df090d062c0821f8c0662a57ccfac8e7660d) states: "no certificate issuance fee is required for dismissals, acquittals, or declinations." This route is an arrest with no charges filed, and this family's own committed manifest describes its evidence as "Any written declination or no-file letter from the prosecutor" — so the route IS the declination case the profile names, and A3's per-route test is satisfied on the route's own terms rather than by analogy. The repository therefore establishes that no certificate issuance fee is required on this route, and the packet's statement that it cannot give an amount and that the participant should ask BCI substitutes a question for an answer the record holds, which A1 forbids in as many words. What passes on this obligation is not in dispute and is recorded so the repair does not disturb it: the court filing fee of $150 is stated and sourced to the row the packet fills on 1044XX page 2, and the court waiver route is named as Utah form 1305GE under Utah Code 78A-2-302 and CJA Rule 4-508.
